function: Joint source-channel coding of images over MIMO: ViT encoder with learned power allocation, ZF plus learned residual equalizer, ViT decoder (p. 5, 7).
system: MxM MIMO, M = 2 by default (up to 4); open-loop CSIR and closed-loop CSIT with SVD precoding; block fading; no RIS; no carrier frequency (p. 3, 8, 14).
method: ViT encoder and decoder with channel heatmap input, trained end to end with MSE plus LPIPS loss; universal variant trained with random SNR (p. 5, 8, 9).
data_channel: Simulated i.i.d. complex Gaussian block-fading MIMO channel with AWGN; Kronecker-correlated in appendix; images: CIFAR10 and ImageNet crops for training, Kodak and CelebA for testing (p. 3, 8, 12, 18).
test_conditions: CIFAR10 50,000 train and 10,000 test; ImageNet crops for training, never-seen Kodak and CelebA for testing; random-SNR training; adaptive-M training over 2 to 4 antennas (p. 8, 10, 14).
baselines: Non-learned: BPG with LDPC and sphere decoding, BPG with capacity-achieving codes and water-filling. Learned: neural codecs MBT2018, Cheng2020, ELIC; CNN and Swin DeepJSCC backbones (p. 8, 9, 11, 13).
metrics: PSNR and LPIPS of reconstructed images versus SNR and bandwidth ratio; model parameters, FLOPs, and encoding/decoding time (p. 3, 11).
complexity: Table IV at Lt = 8: 12.92 M parameters, 0.83 GFLOPs; GPU encoding/decoding 4.82/5.16 ms versus 37.25/71.28 ms for BPG-LDPC on CPU (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 3: "also follow a complex Gaussian distribution with zero mean and variance" - i.i.d. Rayleigh block-fading simulator; p. 18: "the Kronecker channel model [57]" in the appendix; no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing dataset or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "perform well on a never-seen dataset (Kodak)" - trained on ImageNet crops and tested on Kodak and CelebA (p. 12); this is a shift of the source images, not of the channel, and the adaptive-M model is tested on the same M = 2 to 4 it was trained on (p. 14).
q3_support: p. 9: "with the BPG-Capacity and BPG-LDPC schemes at different SNR values" - non-learned separation baselines compared on PSNR and LPIPS; p. 11: "alternative DeepJSCC architectures with different block numbers" - CNN-based and Swin-based DeepJSCC compared on PSNR in Table IV.
q4_support: p. 11: "presents the model size, floating point operations (FLOPs)" - Table IV lists parameters, FLOPs, big-O complexity and encoding and decoding time, 12.92 M parameters and 0.83 GFLOPs at Lt = 8.
q5_support: p. 8: "MIMO system and the CIFAR10 dataset" - source images come from public image datasets (CIFAR10, ImageNet, Kodak, CelebA), which do not count; the channel is simulated and the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: Borderline eligibility (joint source-channel coding): included because the learned method also performs MIMO functions, a learned residual equalizer after ZF that retrieves X' from Y (p. 7) and learned power allocation in the closed loop (p. 5); the main equalization and SVD precoding are model-driven (p. 4). Area 1 chosen over 3 since the paper retrieves the transmitted signal; reviewer to confirm. q2 rests on never-seen image datasets (p. 10, 12). q3 rests on CNN and Swin DeepJSCC backbones (p. 11) and BPG-LDPC with sphere decoding.
